subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike after model v17c-rc2 deploy — mitigation & approval
messages:
From: Carlos Mendoza <carlos@fintegral.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: p95 spike after v17c-rc2 deploy — customer impact

Evelyn / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency on our integration beginning ~2027-08-31 22:00 UTC after the v17c-rc2 model rollout. Our customers are experiencing timeouts and elevated tail latency for multi-turn queries (sequence lengths > 3k). Attaching our p95 export and a condensed trace of a representative request.

Summary:
- Baseline p95 (v16.6): ~180ms
- Observed p95 (v17c-rc2): ~920ms
- Error rate (5xx): increased from 0.2% -> 1.4% in the same window
- Example request id: fin-req-4491 (trace attached)

We can spin up traffic to a fallback model if you need to validate, but this is customer-impacting for several high-value accounts. Please advise next steps and whether you can:
1) authorize an immediate fallback or variant pin for our tenant,
2) provide an ETA for a mitigation/patch, and
3) allow a temporary SLA relief window if needed.

Attachments: p95_export_20270901.csv, trace-20270831.zip

Thanks,
Carlos Mendoza
Head of Platform Engineering
Fintegral
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendoza <carlos@fintegral.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: RE: p95 spike after v17c-rc2 deploy — customer impact

Carlos — thanks for the data and the quick heads up. Monica and I see the same spike in our dashboards for Fintegral. Marcus, can you take a look and confirm root cause? Specifically: is this isolated to the v17c-rc2 variant, and can we fallback customers to an older variant or a quantized variant while you fix?

Customers impacted: Fintegral (high-touch), and our monitoring shows a handful of other tenants on the same pool. Proposed asks for now:
- Immediate temporary mitigation (fallback/pin) for Fintegral if available
- Authorization to request a 48-hour SLA carveout (p95 target relaxed) while engineering validates the fix
- A short public note to Fintegral acknowledging we are on it and outlining the mitigation path

I linked our mutual action plan and the HubSpot record here for tracking: https://drive.google.com/fintegral/mutual-action-plan and https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/Fintegral

Carlos, I’ll keep you copied — we’ll aim to have a clear mitigation proposal within the hour.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendoza <carlos@fintegral.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: p95 spike after v17c-rc2 deploy — customer impact

Quick investigation notes (preliminary):
- Root cause: we’re seeing KV-cache fragmentation and CPU scheduling contention on the host pool when handling long-sequence contexts with v17c-rc2. The new attention optimization in rc2 increases background GC pressure for large KV caches; those GC pauses correlate with p95 spikes.
- Scope: concentrated on pools running v17c-rc2; not all customers are affected, but tenants with heavy mult-turn (>3k tokens) traffic see the worst impact.
- Repro: reproduced with Fintegral payload (fin-req-4491) in staging within 18m of replay. Crash dump attached for reference (crashdump.log).

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Pin Fintegral to the quantized variant model-17c-q8 (same weights, lower runtime mem/latency) — expected p95 down to ~240–320ms, minor quality delta for very long contexts. This is a fast switch (config change).
2) Throttle long-sequence requests at the gateway for affected tenants (60% traffic cap for sequences >3k) — lowers load but requires customer coordination.
3) Canary rollback to v16.6 for critical tenants while we ship rc2.1 (hotfix for KV GC behavior) — will restore baseline latency but loses some rc2 features.

Requesting the following approvals to proceed now:
- Authorization to pin Fintegral to model-17c-q8 immediately
- Approval for a temporary SLA carveout window (48 hours) for Fintegral: relax p95 target from 250ms -> 600ms while mitigation is active
- Permission to initiate a canary rollback to v16.6 for Fintegral if p95 remains >600ms after the quantized pin

If approved, I’ll: apply the pin (5–10 min), monitor metrics for 30m, and create INF-1432 with full telemetry and a timeline for rc2.1.

References: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-1432
Attachments: crashdump.log

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendoza <carlos@fintegral.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: p95 spike after v17c-rc2 deploy — customer impact

Thanks team — approving the mitigation plan with conditions.

Authorization granted (effective immediately):
- Apply model pin: allow Marcus to pin Fintegral to model-17c-q8.
- SLA carveout: approve a 48-hour p95 relaxation window (250ms -> 600ms) for Fintegral only. This is time-bounded and must be rescinded as soon as rc2.1 is validated.
- Canary rollback: authorize rollback to v16.6 for Fintegral if p95 > 600ms after 30m of monitoring post-pin.

Conditions/next steps:
1) Marcus: push the pin and report back in the thread with 30m and 60m snapshots (p50/p95/error rates).
2) Monica/Evelyn: send an honest but concise customer note to Fintegral outlining the mitigation, expected timeline for rc2.1 fix, and the SLA carveout window. Copy legal if we need contract language.
3) Marcus/Infra: prioritize rc2.1 hotfix — target patch within 24 hours.

Carlos — we’ll send the customer note now and implement the pin. We’ll keep you closely updated.

—Ben Carter
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
